questions.q: Explain the nature of the parliamentary executive in India and the position of the President.

answer.text: India has a parliamentary form of executive, adopted from Britain. In this system the executive is not separate from the legislature but is drawn from it and remains responsible to it. The real executive power lies with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, who must enjoy the confidence of the Lok Sabha and fall if they lose it.

The President is the head of state and the constitutional head of the executive, but is only the nominal head. Elected indirectly by an electoral college of elected members of Parliament and state assemblies, the President enjoys wide formal powers on paper. In practice, however, under Article 74 the President must act on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, and this advice is binding.

answer: Thus the President reigns while the Prime Minister rules, which is the essence of the parliamentary system.
